text: Hello.
I'm Dr. Kimberly Armstrong,
superintendent of Portland Public
Schools. On Tuesday, October 6th, I will
present to the school board some options
for how we can bring more stability to
our district and give our students the
best opportunities to succeed in the
future.
Included in those scenarios will be
proposals for some school consolidations
and closures. This is one of the most
difficult tasks that I have faced in my
entire tenure as superintendent and
certainly as an educator.
I know our neighborhood schools aren't
just for learning. They are beloved
community hubs and touchstones where
families gather regularly. Whether it's
watching an evening talent show or
connecting with other parents on the
playground.
And we have reached a point where we
must make changes.
School enrollments are declining and
have been for several years
>> [snorts]
>> due to factors beyond our control for
better part of a decade.
We have been taking resources from some
schools and subsidizing others. This is
simply not sustainable. We must
right-size
our district by balancing enrollment and
resources throughout our schools so we
can give every student the best possible
education.
So let me be clear. While no one,
especially not me or the board, wants to
close any school, enrollment is going to
continue to decline and at least for
now, funding is not going to increase.
Doing nothing will further stretch
limited resources and cause reductions
in programs and staffing. That would be
irresponsible and unfair to our
students.
Now is our chance to make positive
changes to benefit our students, our
educators, and our entire community long
into the future.

>> This is the first in a series of videos
that I hope will help you understand why
we're facing this challenge, why we must
make these difficult decisions, and how
we're doing it.
The scenarios will we present on October
6 are not final decisions. They are the
start of a real conversation with
multiple opportunities to learn more and
participate in the process.
The school board will vote on the issue
in December. And I understand that
changes of this nature and magnitude can
be scary or unsettling or both.
We'll continue to share information and
updates throughout this process.
You can also learn more and submit
comments by going to pps.net
and clicking on right-sizing.
Thank you.
